baseline: UX-DESIGN-FREEZE-01, DB18, and atomic action audit 2026-09-18

state_definitions.live: A visible control reaches its production query or command and returns a user-facing result.
state_definitions.partial: Some of the contracted operation is live, but a required state, command, return, or recovery path is absent.
state_definitions.presentation_only: The UI demonstrates the intended presentation with local or fixture state but does not execute the operation.
state_definitions.unavailable: The UI exposes a disabled or unavailable control for an operation required by the accepted contract.
state_definitions.missing: The accepted operation has no discoverable UI control.

operations.label: Find a Project

evidence.boundary: Real disposable PostgreSQL plus focused authenticated route and renderer-neutral typed-client tests prove bounded server-owned Project search across current name, Objective statement, and registered profile label; status/profile filters; validated pagination; exact query/result binding; and visible failure semantics. The frozen React Find control still filters its loaded page locally, so design-owned binding and browser execution remain outstanding.

operations.runtime_owner: GET /api/queries/projects -> ProjectShellViewReader.searchProjectShellViews -> PostgresProjectShellViewReader (REPEATABLE READ current Project/ProjectDefinition/Objective authority)

operations.label: Open a Project

evidence.boundary: Real disposable PostgreSQL, the production HTTP server, bearer authentication, and ProjectShellClient prove that one exact representative member returned by GET /api/queries/projects resolves through GET /api/queries/projects/:projectId/shell to the same Project, ProjectDefinition, current Objective, and Open Brief destination. This backend trace does not invoke the visible Open Brief control and makes no browser-navigation claim; that execution remains design-owned.

operations.runtime_owner: GET /api/queries/projects -> ProjectShellViewReader.searchProjectShellViews -> PostgresProjectShellViewReader; GET /api/queries/projects/:projectId/shell -> ProjectShellViewReader.getProjectShellView -> PostgresProjectShellViewReader (authenticated REPEATABLE READ current Project/ProjectDefinition/Objective authority)

operations.label: Switch Projects

evidence.boundary: Real disposable PostgreSQL, the production HTTP server, bearer authentication, and ProjectShellClient prove that selecting a different exact collection member resolves that Project's server-owned shell and Brief fallback while the prior Project's immutable retained Graph task and running Work remain independently unchanged. This backend trace does not invoke the visible Project switcher or prove browser-local draft, selection, focus, history, or return-context preservation; that visible DB18-P11 execution remains design-owned.

operations.runtime_owner: GET /api/queries/projects -> ProjectShellViewReader.searchProjectShellViews -> PostgresProjectShellViewReader; GET /api/queries/projects/:projectId/shell -> ProjectShellViewReader.getProjectShellView -> PostgresProjectShellViewReader (authenticated REPEATABLE READ per-Project shell, server-owned resume/Brief destination, retained ProjectInquiry and Work isolation)

Create a Project with a registered profile

evidence.boundary: Real disposable PostgreSQL, the production HTTP server, bearer authentication, ProjectProfileClient, and ProjectShellClient prove exact registered-profile selection and Project/definition/objective/focus creation, canonical receipt persistence, Brief destination, idempotent replay, unknown-effect assessment, confirmed recovery, and preservation of an unrelated Project. operations.label: Import or reuse a Project with preserved ancestry

evidence.boundary: The same authenticated production trace assesses the exact create request before submission as outcome_unknown with only the server-registered idempotent retry and safe Projects fallback, then reassesses its retained receipt as effect_confirmed with exact Project and Brief return without a second mutation. This backend trace does not invoke the visible Recover Project control or cover the complete adverse-state scenario.

operations.runtime_owner: POST /api/queries/project-profile-command-recovery -> PostgresProjectProfileRuntime; eligible retry delegates to the existing idempotent create/reset command owner

operations.label: Navigate to a Project place with context

evidence.boundary: Real disposable PostgreSQL, the production HTTP server, bearer authentication, and ProjectShellClient prove that repeated Project-place context reads retain one exact Project, registered definition, current Objective, authority position, projection state, attention, supported-place order, and honest place summaries. The server rejects a client-supplied place override because browser place selection is presentation state, not backend authority. This trace does not invoke Project navigation, change a browser route, preserve browser-local focus or selection, or prove return to origin; those visible SP02 and UX-FLOW-07 behaviors remain design-owned.

operations.runtime_owner: GET /api/queries/projects/:projectId/shell -> ProjectShellViewReader.getProjectShellView -> PostgresProjectShellViewReader (authenticated REPEATABLE READ Project context and registered place summaries); the browser router owns place selection and visible navigation

interaction_definitions.query: Reads exact production state without an authority effect.
interaction_definitions.navigation: Changes place or context while preserving exact identity, state, and return.
